title: Landing page
slide_intent: Show how a landing page can introduce an unfamiliar promise, then let the visitor inspect how it works. Each viewport needs a clear next action.
strategic_value: Halfkey can connect its promise of limited authority to a visible allowance. The landing page gives the visitor a chance to understand what writing a key means before proceeding.
demonstration: Two browser views pair a pale hero with a dark first-scroll explanation. A weekly purchase instruction, a dot figure and the resulting key details connect the visitor’s words to the product.
practical_value: A designer can decide which content to expose in the hero and which explanation to reveal on the first scroll.

content_islands.name: Running header and title
content_islands.spec: Place the page identity at the top and set “Landing page” above two side-by-side browser frames.

content_islands.name: Hero
content_islands.spec: Label the left frame Hero. Place “Give it half the key.”, the wallet description and the blue Get Halfkey action on the left. Put the full-size dot disc on the right, with three smaller key examples in a strip below.

content_islands.name: First scroll
content_islands.spec: Label the right frame First scroll. Use a dark ground and the headline “Write a limit in plain words. See it drawn as a key.” Align the instruction card, dot disc and key fields in one row. Place three numbered explanations below.

content_islands.name: Implementation notes
content_islands.spec: Place four aligned notes below the frames. Cover the live disc spending $40 on scroll, the single blue action, continuity with the waitlist mechanic, and web typography.
